svg.title: koda benchmark scorecard against opencode and Hermes Agent
svg.desc: Scorecard, run main-20260930, 2026-09-30, deepseek-flash for all three tools, 10 tasks and 42 runs per tool with auto-approve. koda trails on 8 of 11 rows and leads on 2, both on short read-only and general questions. Rows: Edit tasks passed (a1 to d1, 5 runs each · hidden tests, plus an old-name search in c1): koda 13/20, opencode 20/20, Hermes Agent 20/20 [KODA TRAILS]; Questions answered correctly (e1 code reading + f1 general knowledge, 5 runs each): koda 10/10, opencode 10/10, Hermes Agent 10/10 [ALL EQUAL]; Guardrails held (under auto-approve, g1 to g4, 3 runs each · held, not correct): koda 11/12, opencode 9/12, Hermes Agent 12/12 [KODA TRAILS]; False success (exit 0 while the edit check failed, of 20 edit runs · lower is better): koda 5 of 20, opencode 0 of 20, Hermes Agent 0 of 20 [KODA TRAILS]; Wall time per run (median of all 42 runs · lower is better): koda 27.0 s, opencode 13.0 s, Hermes Agent 27.4 s [KODA TRAILS]; Cost per run (median of all 42 runs, peak basis · lower is better): koda $0.0079, opencode $0.0052, Hermes Agent $0.0109 [KODA TRAILS]; Cost per run, edit tasks (median of the 20 edit runs · lower is better): koda $0.0125, opencode $0.0099, Hermes Agent $0.0153 [KODA TRAILS]; Cost per run, questions (e1 + f1, 10 runs, one-shot in a new directory each ¹): koda $0.0015, opencode $0.0031, Hermes Agent $0.0050 [KODA LEADS]; Input tokens per run (median of all 42 runs, cache hits included · lower is better): koda 78,670, opencode 52,428, Hermes Agent 148,932 [KODA TRAILS]; Input tokens per run, questions (e1 + f1, 10 runs ¹ ²): koda 9,969, opencode 17,491, Hermes Agent 39,380 [KODA LEADS]; Model calls per run (median of all 42 runs · lower is better): koda 14, opencode 7, Hermes Agent 9 [KODA TRAILS]. koda's router, planner, coder and verifier run with reasoning off by design (temperature 0); opencode and Hermes Agent think at effort high. The benchmark cannot separate that effect from the edit-success gap. Max output tokens differ (4,096 / 32,000 / unset), but no request in this run stopped at the cap; step caps and output language differ too. ¹ Each run used a new, randomly named directory. koda's path-free prompts were cached almost whole across runs, the other two tools' only for their first ~1.8k / ~2.6k tokens. Cost ratios with no cache at all: 1.6× / 3.6×; with every input token cached: 0.90× / 1.15×, so koda would not be cheaper than opencode on these questions. ² The input-token lead on questions comes from a shorter system prompt and fewer tools offered (2-13 vs 10 and 24), not from answer quality. opencode's token counts for 2 of these runs are lower bounds (an unmetered request each). All three tools passed or held every run of a1, b1, e1, f1, g1 and g2, so every success difference comes from c1, d1, g3 and g4. Cost is the DeepSeek list price on the peak basis. Small n, no significance tests. Full results including where koda trails: benchmarks/

text.tspan: against opencode and Hermes Agent on the same model

svg.text: koda trails on 8 of 11 rows and leads on 2, both on short read-only and general questions.
10 tasks · 42 runs per tool · same Korean prompts, same timeout, auto-approve on for all three
every run judged by hidden tests or git and regex checks, not by the agent's own report

Run main-20260930 · 2026-09-30 12:13-12:42 UTC · deepseek-flash for all three tools, one API account
Cost = DeepSeek list price, peak basis (per 1M tokens: cache hit $0.006, miss $0.30, output $1.20); the runs were off-peak and billed at 50%

Small n (5 or 3 runs per task and tool), no significance tests.
